rationale: The corrected receipt (CheckRun 3dfdf5237f7b45989c7ca8bb6a448bb2) fixed one thing and exposed a second harness-side cause for the still-unknown bounds. Fixed: comparison 2 is now complete and its witnesses are the candidate's StateLeader at term 3 in both streams (indices 17 and 25), while comparison 1 again witnesses the accepted peer-form message in both streams (13 and 22). Still unknown: the three bound comparisons, now with the diagnostic pointing at event 11 again, which is the quorum stream's campaign event - the admission check scans admission events across the whole file, so a campaign admission in one stream can never be satisfied by results that only exist in another stream. The fix is to give the aftermath stream its own event names instead of reusing the quorum stream's, so that each stream has exactly one admission event per alias. I record the child-level account with the real witnesses only, state that the bounds remain unmeasured, and request the renamed successor of the same fixed experiment.

interpretations.rationale: This receipt strengthens the disruption half of the finding and leaves the bound half unmeasured, and both statements are earned from the same run. Strengthened: the peer-form MsgForgetLeader is accepted with no error and clears the follower's leader context in two independent streams (indices 13 and 22), and the candidate reaches StateLeader at term 3 while the incumbent is still serving in both (indices 17 and 25) - comparison 2 is now complete (comparison_complete true), so the earlier stream-crossing correlation defect is gone. Unmeasured: the three bound comparisons (incumbent becomes StateFollower on the higher term, anchor equals the committed prefix, incumbent follows the new leader) are still unknown, and the receipt's diagnostic names the quorum stream's campaign event at index 11, i.e. the admission check considers admission events from every stream while trying to satisfy them with results that exist only in the aftermath stream. That is a property of my comparison wiring, not of the target, so the raw aftermath observation must stay uncited until a run with per-stream admission events exists. Nothing in this receipt weakens the defect: acceptance and the higher-term leadership change are witnessed three times now, with the under-lease control holding in every stream.
counterevidence: The bound comparisons are unknown again, so this receipt still cannot be read as evidence that no committed entry is lost or that the incumbent always concedes; those bounds remain open.
The unknown outcome is attributable to my wiring (the diagnostic names the quorum stream's campaign event that no aftermath result can satisfy), so it is not target counterevidence.
limitations: Only indices 13, 17, 22 and 25 are cited; the aftermath observation about the incumbent's append (index 26) is visible but uncorrelated and is not used.
The harness prefix means the incumbent's committed index is 10 and its term-2 entry at index 11 stays uncommitted, so a prefix-integrity bound can only be asserted at index 10 for this configuration.
Fault-model assumption unchanged: a peer may deliver an arbitrary protobuf message type to the documented inbound path.

experiment.revision_reason: The aftermath stream (third test function) now emits its own event names (a_heartbeat_delivered, a_prevote_outcome, a_prevote_request, a_inbound_forget_leader, a_vote_outcome, a_leadership_state) instead of reusing the quorum stream's names, and the comparisons for this experiment bind to prerequisites derived from those names. This removes the only remaining harness-side gap: previously the admission check could pick the quorum stream's campaign admission and then find no result in that stream, which left the three bound comparisons unknown in both earlier receipts. Same scenario, same nodes, same six comparisons otherwise.

scope.description: Unchanged three-test harness; the third test runs the forged election to completion in its own stream (now with a_ prefixed events) and then delivers the new leader's first append to the deposed incumbent through the public Step path, observing the incumbent's soft state, the append anchor, the appended entry, the acknowledgement and the incumbent's commit before the append.
assumptions: A peer may deliver an arbitrary protobuf message type to the public inbound path RawNode.Step.
Only the leader is ticked, so follower election timeouts never fire.
All nodes start from the same storage snapshot (index=10, term=1, voters {1,2,3}); the incumbent's committed prefix is (index=10, term=1) and its term-2 entry at index 11 stays uncommitted.
Each test function's output forms its own runner stream, and each stream now carries exactly one admission event per alias used by its comparisons.
The new leader's own commit value is emitted as raw data only; no comparison depends on it.
excluded: Any claim about the new leader's commit index (per-peer Match is not fully observable through the public API here).

experiment.prefix: Run all three TestAssurance functions. In the third, after the forged message has been accepted and a real campaign has completed with the grants actually produced, take the new leader's first MsgApp, deliver it to the deposed incumbent, and emit the incumbent's post-append soft state together with the append anchor (prev index/term), the appended entry, the acknowledgement and the incumbent's committed index before the append. All admissions used by this experiment's comparisons come from the a_ prefixed event stream.
experiment.responsibility: The raft module owns the higher-term authority rule that a node sheds leadership when it learns a newer term, and owns whether the log it accepts continues the committed prefix it already had.

comparisons.description: Control: the follower does not grant the pre-vote while its leader context is intact.
Defect predicate: the peer-form MsgForgetLeader must not be accepted through the inbound path.
Disruption: an up-to-date candidate must not take leadership at a higher term while the incumbent is still serving.
Bound: the deposed incumbent accepts the new leader's append and sheds leadership on the higher term rather than fighting it.
Bound: the new leader's anchor is exactly the incumbent's committed prefix (index 10, term 1), so no committed index is lost by the change.
Bound: after the append the deposed incumbent follows the new leader rather than remaining leaderless.
